questions.question: Why is backing with a trailer dangerous?

options.text: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front of the vehicle.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.
Trailers are not made to be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver cannot see behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only drive in reverse when absolutely necessary.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact.
Ignore their gestures.
Try to race.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignore their gestures.
questions.explanation: Do not let an aggressive driver provoke you. Avoid eye contact and do not try to race them.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Prohibited.
Acceptable if weather conditions are clear.
Permitted if use is work-related.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited.
questions.explanation: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a driving hazard?

options.text: An accident on the roadway
An open road
A police car helping a motorist on the side of the road
An ice cream truck

questions.correctAnswerText: An open road
questions.explanation: Accidents distract drivers. Ice cream trucks attract children who may not watch for traffic. An open road is safe, not a hazard.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Stay in their path.
Make eye contact with the driver.
Make gestures at the driver.
Report the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Report the driver.
questions.explanation: Get out of their way and avoid eye contact. Do not gesture at them. Report them to authorities when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: A bus should be refueled:

options.text: Inside a closed building while passengers are on board.
In any location while passengers are on board.
Without passengers on board, unless absolutely necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Without passengers on board, unless absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus with passengers on board unless it is absolutely necessary. Never refuel inside an enclosed building with passengers on board.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.
Discouraged.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder because you cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare affects vision, and more tired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT indicate bad brakes?

options.text: Cracked drums
Pads free of oil or grease
Very thin shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Check for cracked drums, pads covered in oil or grease, and worn or broken pads. Clean pads without oil or grease are a sign of good brakes.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: You should move your vehicle quickly.
You should move your vehicle slowly.
The move should be made with a jerking motion.
You do not need to use a turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should move your vehicle slowly.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move and helps you keep control. Always use your turn signal.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should never be done.
Should be done to prevent cargo from shifting.
Can only be done with metal pieces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done to prevent cargo from shifting.
questions.explanation: Block cargo on its front, back, and sides to keep it from moving during transport.

questions.question: What happens with a broken exhaust system?

options.text: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
It does not cause problems.
It should not be a concern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes can enter the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system lets poisonous fumes into the vehicle's cabin. Check your exhaust system regularly for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: After you start a trip with cargo, what should you do?

options.text: You do not need to inspect the cargo.
Inspect the cargo only if it is making noise.
Inspect the cargo only if there is an obvious problem.
Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the cargo after 50 miles to make sure it is still secure.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles.

questions.question: When should you watch for black ice?

options.text: When it is snowing.
When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
When the temperature is above freezing and there is snow on the ground.
Just after a rainstorm.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it. Watch for black ice when the temperature is below freezing and the road looks wet.

questions.question: What should the overhead inside mirror show?

options.text: The outside of the driver's side of the bus.
All of the students on the bus.
Students in the first four rows of the bus.
In front of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the students on the bus.
questions.explanation: Adjust the overhead inside mirror to show all students on the bus. This includes students sitting right behind the driver.

questions.question: What do over-length loads require?

options.text: Special permits.
Roads to be closed to other traffic.
A person to walk alongside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Special permits.
questions.explanation: Over-length, over-width, and overweight loads need special permits from the Department of Transportation.

questions.question: How far in advance of a school bus stop should the bus turn on its lights?

options.text: 2 to 4 seconds.
5 to 10 seconds.
45 seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 to 10 seconds.
questions.explanation: Turn on the flashing amber warning lights at least 200 feet before stopping. This is about 5 to 10 seconds ahead, unless state law says otherwise.

questions.question: What should you do after a bus trip is completed?

options.text: Return the bus without an inspection.
Inspect the bus.
Drain the fuel from the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inspect the bus.
questions.explanation: Inspect the bus at the end of every trip. Passengers may damage safety items. An inspection finds damage so it can be fixed before the next trip.

questions.question: What do move over laws require?

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move to the left lane if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is stopped on the side of the road, move out of the lane next to it if you can do so safely. If you cannot move over safely, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: Why should you cover cargo?

options.text: To protect it from thieves.
To protect it from weather.
To prevent other drivers from seeing what is being transported.
To keep it a secret.

questions.correctAnswerText: To protect it from weather.
questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people if it spills and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to affect the body?

options.text: After only one drink.
After several drinks have been consumed.
At the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: After only one drink.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects muscle control, reaction time, vision, judgment, and inhibition. Some people show signs of impairment after just one drink. It is safest not to drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.
